_comment: URL PATHS AS A CAMPAIGN IDENTIFIER. Standard clustering assumes the operator's identity lives in the HOSTNAME — the domain, the subdomain, the certificate. A mature kit operator inverts that: they buy a pool of disposable, meaningless hosts (numeric labels on cheap TLDs) and select which branded scam template to serve using the URL PATH. `host-a/<kit-x>/`, `host-b/<kit-x>/`, `host-c/<kit-y>/` is one operator running two kits across three hosts — but every host-level artifact differs, so host-level clustering sees three unrelated sites and path-blind collection throws away the one field that ties them together. This file holds everything that layer matches against: how a path is normalised, which segments are VARIABLE (so two paths that differ only by a session id collapse to one template), which are GENERIC (so `/login` never becomes a fingerprint), and how much of a path is worth keeping. The unit of investigation becomes host+path, not host. Nothing here is case data — these are generic web conventions.

variable_patterns._comment: Segment patterns that are VARIABLE — a session id, a build hash, a per-victim token, a date. Each is replaced by its placeholder when building a path TEMPLATE, so `/kit/9f3a1c/step2` and `/kit/44b0de/step2` collapse to one template instead of looking like two campaigns. Order matters: the first match wins, so the specific patterns come before the loose ones. `regex` is matched case-insensitively against ONE whole segment. Add a pattern when a case shows the operator randomising a segment you are otherwise clustering on; do NOT add one so loose it eats the kit name (a pattern matching any 6-letter word would erase exactly the segment this layer exists to keep).

generic_segments._comment: THE BASE-RATE CONTROL, and the most important list in this file. These segments appear on millions of unrelated sites, so a shared one is worth nothing as a same-operator link — clustering on `/login` or `/assets` would fuse the entire internet into one operator. A path whose every meaningful segment is in this list emits NO kit pivot at all. This is the same discipline as the generic subdomain labels and the parked-favicon denylist: count the population before calling a value a fingerprint. Add a segment here the moment a run produces a cluster joined only by it.

locale_segments._comment: Language / country segments. A kit operator localises one template per market, so `/<locale>/<kit>` and `/<kit>-<locale>` are both common shapes. These are normalised to `{locale}` in the TEMPLATE (so the same kit in five markets is recognised as one kit) but the concrete value is KEPT separately as the campaign's target-market evidence — which market a template was built for is a finding, not noise. Two-letter codes only here; a longer language name is treated as an ordinary segment.

kit_thresholds._comment: How much of a path is worth keeping, and when a segment is distinctive enough to be a KIT NAME. `min_kit_len` rejects one- and two-character segments (they are routing noise, not names). `max_segments` bounds the template so a deep CMS URL cannot become a unique 'fingerprint' that matches only itself. `max_kit_len` rejects an absurdly long segment (usually an encoded blob the variable patterns missed). `min_hosts_for_pattern` is the analyst-facing threshold quoted by the path-pattern report: below it, a repeated path is an observation, not yet a pattern — the same base-rate discipline applied to the operator's own estate.

asset_extensions._comment: Extensions that make a segment a STATIC FILE rather than a template directory. Without this rule the last segment of `/assets/js/app.js` survives the generic-segment denylist (because `app.js` is not itself a common word) and gets emitted as a kit name — a fingerprint on a filename every bundler in the world produces. Page extensions (.php, .html, .aspx) are deliberately ABSENT: a kit's entry point is often exactly `/<brand>.html`, and dropping those would discard the artifact this layer exists to keep.

index_files._comment: Trailing filenames that mean 'the directory itself' and are stripped when normalising, so `/kit/`, `/kit/index.html` and `/kit/index.php` are recognised as ONE location rather than three. Only add a name that is genuinely a directory-index default; stripping a real page name would merge two distinct templates.
